site_name: The White House,  Harrow On The Hill Campus  Lowlands Road
description:
Listed building consent:
internal and external alterations, demolition works and extensions to
accommodate a change of use of an educational building (Use Class F1a) to a
community health hub (Use Class E(e)) comprising GP surgeries and primary
healthcare facilities, including insertion of front ground floor window,
staircase alterations, insertion of lift, front extension following demolition
of front conservatory, fire safety works including door alterations,
insulation, secondary glazing, installation of services, basement waterproofing
and access works, relocation of historic steps on the ground floor, removal of
an existing ground floor window and alteration of the structural opening to
create a new door opening, insertion of security gate on ground floor.
decision_conditions:
<p>Ground Floor Wall: The historic wall between rooms G02 and G03 is to be reinstated within 3 months of 
the date of this consent.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Site Meeting: Before the start of works, a site meeting shall be held between the Local Planning 
Authority Conservation Officer and the persons responsible for undertaking the 
works to ensure that the conditions attached to the Listed Building Consent are 
understood and can be complied with in full. Notification of the date and time of a 
meeting shall be made in writing to, and agreed by, the Local Planning Authority. 
The minutes of the meeting shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the 
Local Planning Authority before the start of works.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Unknown evidence or features: During the works, if unknown evidence or hidden historic features are revealed this 
shall be retained in-situ. Works shall be halted in the relevant area of the building 
and the Local Planning Authority shall be notified immediately. Failure to do so may 
result in unauthorised works being carried out and an offence being committed.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Services: Notwithstanding the plans hereby approved, before relevant work begins a method 
statement for the position, type and method of installation of all new and relocated 
services and related fixtures (including any proposed new ceiling linings) for each 
floor plan and an appraisal of how the proposal will impact on any historic fabric 
(including detail of any new notching of beams and perforations to walls, floors and 
ceilings), shall be specified (and include drawings as appropriate) and agreed in 
writing with the Local Planning Authority wherever these installations are to be 
visible, or where ducts or other methods of concealment are proposed. The works 
shall be implemented only in accordance with such approval.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Making Good: All new external and internal works and finishes and works of making good to the 
retained fabric shall match the existing adjacent work with regard to the methods 
used and to material, colour, texture and profile, unless shown otherwise on the 
drawings or other documentation hereby approved or required by any conditions(s) 
attached to this consent.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Doors: Notwithstanding the approved plans and supporting documents, the following 
historic doors (including doorframes, fanlights, architraves, ironmongery, glazing, 
fixtures and fittings), namely G10.ED01 (also called G10.W04), G14.ED01 (also 
called G15.ED01), G12.D01, G12.D04 (also called G16.D01), G02.ED01, G09.D01, 
G11.D01, door to room F09, F01.ED01, F07:D01 and door S01.D01, shall not be 
removed, altered, relocated or replaced until the following has been submitted to, 
and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority: a significance assessment 
prepared by a suitably qualified heritage specialist; a condition survey; details of all 
proposed repair, retention, relocation, reuse, replacement and fire upgrading 
measures; and clear and convincing justification for the loss, alteration or 
replacement of any historic fabric, including consideration of alternative approaches 
and opportunities for retention, repair and reuse. Existing and proposed plans, 
elevations and details shall also be provided where appropriate. The approved 
details shall thereafter be implemented in full.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Wall Between Room F10 and F09: Details for the retention of a downstand and side nib of the wall between room F10 
and F09, with some of its historic wallpaper retained is to be provided to, and 
approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority prior to the removal of this wall, 
where not interfering with the proposed lift. The works shall thereafter be 
undertaken and retained as approved.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Treatment Area Enclosures: Prior to the installation of any fixtures to accommodate these, full details of the 
proposed fixtures in relation to an assessment of the significance of the fabric 
affected by a suitable specialist are to be provided to, and approved in writing by, 
the Local Planning Authority. Submission of scaled existing and proposed plans and 
elevations shall also be submitted where appropriate. The approved details shall be 
implemented in full.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Two former external windows: Notwithstanding the approved plans and supporting documents, prior to the 
commencement of works affecting the two former external windows enclosed by the 
conservatory, details shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local 
Planning Authority. The submission shall include an assessment of opportunities for 
retention, repair, recording, reuse and interpretation of the historic fabric. The 
approved details shall thereafter be implemented in full.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Principal Staircase: Notwithstanding the approved plans and supporting documents, details for the 
following should be provided to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning 
Authority prior to the start of the relevant part of the work; </p><p>
a) The proposed alterations to the principal staircase balustrades and handrail for 
improved health and safety.  
b) Proposed repairs. 
             The above should each include a report by a suitable specialist that includes an 
assessment of the significance of the staircase, full details of the proposal (including 
scaled drawings as appropriate) and an understanding of how what is proposed is 
the minimum, reversible and most subtle of work that retains historic fabric and 
meets health and safety obligations.</p>

<p>Basement Waterproof Tanking: Details for the proposed basement waterproofing, including technical report 
showing how the significance and breathability of the building would be retained and 
scaled existing and proposed drawings, should be provided to, and approved in 
writing by, the Local Planning Authority prior to the commencement of the relevant 
part of the works. 
              The works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and 
thereafter retained.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Wall between room F07 and F10:&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; Notwithstanding the approved plans, no works shall take place to the wall between 
rooms F07 and F10 until details of its significance by a suitable specialist, together 
with a detailed method statement that includes every effort to retain, reuse and 
repair this historic wall, and historic fabric components, as closely as possible to its 
current state and location (including consideration of alternatives), any proposed 
recording, and clear and convincing justification for any harm to heritage 
significance, have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning 
Authority. The approved details shall thereafter be implemented in full.&nbsp;</p>
